One product · three levels of depth
Every part follows the work.

  
RailCall starts as your everyday AI conversation. The work you repeat becomes a capability your team can keep, run, inspect, and improve.

  

    
01 / CHAT
Use it once.
Answers, drafts, analysis, and running saved workflows. Most people can stay here.

    
02 / BUILDER
Make it repeatable.
Edit the steps behind a conversation. Save a version with its connections, inputs, and approval rules.

    
03 / STUDIO
See what happened.
The existing Studio inspects execution, routing, permissions, and cryptographic receipts.

  

  
Workflows are things you keep.
Builder is their editor. Run them from Chat or a configured trigger. Every run points back to the workflow version and conversation.
NFTs belong to creator publishing.
An optional token can reference a workflow version and its creator record. It is separate from the receipt of a particular run. No wallet is needed for everyday use.

  
The engine travels with the work.
RailCall-operated servers make the browser useful immediately. Desktop moves eligible steps to your machine. Approved external model APIs handle the steps that need more capability. The task, workflow, and evidence remain linked.

  
Marketplace supplies the building blocks.
Discover workflows and modules, inspect their permissions, then make them your own.
Railhub supports the organization.
24/7 uptime, internal capacity routing, a centralized cryptographic ledger, and a shared workflow library. Explore here or visit Railhub.ai.

Evidence follows every run
A signature you can check.

  
Production receipts should bind the task, workflow version, policy, route, tool results, and measured cost. The executor signs; Studio and independent tools verify using the public key.

  
Desktop execution
Your runtime signs its steps with its local key. The private key stays on your device.
Hosted execution
RailCall's execution service signs its steps with protected server keys. A combined receipt links local and hosted evidence.

  
Signed synthetic specimen
This bundled example has a real Ed25519 signature from a temporary demonstration key. It proves integrity of this example, not that production work happened.
Try changing a signed field to see verification fail.

  
A signature establishes integrity and key possession. Trust in the executor, provider usage evidence, key identity, and completeness are separate questions. No blockchain transaction is needed to verify a receipt. Ed25519 specification ↗



  
Optional creator publishing
Give a workflow a provenance record.

  
Keep a useful workflow as a versioned asset. An optional NFT can reference its package hash and creator metadata. Run receipts still remain separate, recording each use.

  

  
Concept preview only: no wallet, mint, token transfer, or public registration occurs. A token record does not itself grant file access or settle licensing; explicit license terms and access controls must accompany a release. NFT token and metadata standard ↗
